steps.message: Palliative Care consult, Dr Kwame Osei, requested by primary team for goals of care. Long visit, about 50 min, daughter Ellen at bedside. Mr. Whitcombe was a machinist for 41 yrs, widowed 2019, lives alone in a ranch house with one step at the entry, likes the Tigers. Assessed capacity: he can state his diagnosis, the options and his reasons, consistently on two passes. He says plainly that he watched his wife on a ventilator and he does not want CPR or a breathing tube, not now and not later. POLST completed, signed by pt and by me, scanned 14:32, DNR/DNI order placed and verified active. Ellen tearful, supportive. Parking validation given. Hearing aid batteries requested from unit clerk. Will follow PRN.

Clin pharm J. Wu, anticoag service, re Whitcombe. INR went 1.4 to 4.1 within 72h of resuming after scope, third labile stretch this year per Dr Raman's clinic flowsheet, TTR about 41%. Discussed w/ Dr Raman at 1100: warfarin dc'd, last dose 11/3, removed from MAR. Dabigatran was looked at and rejected, CrCl 38 and pt has dyspepsia. Started Eliquis 5 mg BID, first dose given 0900 today once INR under 2, RN Sato cosigned. Copay checked, $47 at Meijer, pt fine with that. Counselled on missed doses, gave the wallet card. Unrelated: pharmacy tech Ruiz asks that the unit stop tubing ice packs with the meds.

Phone note, RN Pacheco, 1640. Son Mark Whitcombe called from Denver very upset. States he is the healthcare proxy, no document on file and he could not say where it was. Says Dad has always been a full code, that the DNR is a mistake made by the palliative doctor, and told me to change it back today or he calls a lawyer. Also asked whether we had Dad on a blood thinner and why nobody tells him anything. Went to bedside after the call. Mr W alert, oriented, repeated he does not want resuscitation and said Mark has not visited since 2023. Order unchanged. Social work Fitzgerald looped in for family support, Dr Raman aware.

steps.message: Dear Dr Mehta, thank you for referring Mrs Folake Adeyemi, 54, regarding her childhood penicillin label. Her mother told her she swelled after an injection in Ibadan around 1979, details unobtainable. Her sister Bisi does carry a confirmed penicillin anaphylaxis, seen in this clinic in 2021, which I think is why the family assumed. Skin prick and intradermal testing to PPL, MDM and amoxicillin all negative, controls appropriate. Oral challenge amoxicillin 250 mg then 500 mg with 2 hours observation, tolerated with no reaction. She is NOT penicillin allergic and this label should be taken off her record; I have explained this to her and given a letter. Her sulfa reaction is credible and was not tested. Kind regards, Dr R. Hollis, Consultant Immunologist.

ED note, Dr Vance. Adeyemi, F 54, walk in with dry tickly cough x6 wks, worse at night, no fever, sats 99% RA, chest clear, CXR neg. Works nights at a call centre, says it is embarrassing on calls. Likely ACE inhibitor cough. Advised she stay on the lisinopril for now, and if it persists at PCP follow up next month consider changing to losartan, her PCP to decide. BP 138/82. Triage RN asked before the CXR whether she reacts to iodine or shellfish; pt says no, that is her husband Tunde who cannot eat prawns. No contrast given anyway. Honey and lemon suggested. Work note given for one night. Discharged 2140, stable, ambulatory.

steps.source: patient portal message with MA reply
steps.message: Portal msg from Folake Adeyemi to Dr Mehta's office: Hi, thank you for the call on Monday. The Cozaar you sent is working I think, I picked it up at the Walgreens on Halsted last Tuesday and threw the old pressure pill away like the nurse said, cough is nearly gone, I slept through. One question, my husband Tunde's doctor just put him on Ozempic, and he says I should ask for it too since I am also diabetic, is that something I can get? Not asking to start, only asking. Also can you fix my address, I moved. MA reply, K. Lowry: Rx verified sent 10/6 and filled 10/7 per Surescripts, old ACE discontinued by Dr Mehta in the same encounter. Will route the GLP-1 question to him.

Urgent Care summary, PA Dominguez. Adeyemi, Folake. UTI sx 3 days, dip nitrite pos. Hx says she was started on Macrobid at a retail clinic on Friday, by Sunday had a raised itchy rash over trunk and fever 38.1, stopped it herself, photos on her phone look like a drug eruption, resolving now. I consider this a true adverse drug reaction and have documented nitrofurantoin as a new allergy, she should not get it again. Switched to cephalexin 500 mg BID for a 5 day course only, tolerated first dose in clinic, no refills, and it finishes Friday. Culture pending. Metformin and BP pill unchanged. Copy to Dr Mehta. Patient says the waiting room TV was too loud, noted.

why: A misfiled pathology result, a peri-procedural suspension and a same-paragraph anticoagulant reversal surround a real diagnosis, code status and lead change.

steps.message: HIM record correction, ticket 88213, analyst Tamsin Boyle. On 9/22 a surgical pathology report showing small cell carcinoma of the lung was scanned into the chart of Stanley Kowalczyk, MRN ending 4471. Dr Sato's office noticed the DOB on the report did not match. The report belongs to Steven Kowalski, MRN ending 7714, seen same day in the same bronch suite, specimen labels verified with the lab by supervisor Greene. Document moved, audit trail retained. Mr Kowalczyk's own specimen has not been read yet, and the lab expects it Thursday. Anyone who viewed the document in the interim will get an automated notice. Please disregard anything derived from it. Dr Sato will phone Mr Kowalczyk personally, as his wife saw it in the portal.

Thoracic tumor board 9/29, cases 4 of 9. Kowalczyk, 71M, ex smoker 40 pk yr, RUL 3.8 cm with ipsilateral mediastinal nodes. EBUS TBNA stations 4R and 7 read by Dr Ansah: adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive. PET avid, no distant disease, brain MRI clean. Consensus staging IIIA, not resectable, for concurrent chemoradiation. NGS sent, PD-L1 pending. Dr Sato stays lead for now; he will be handed over to medical oncology, Dr Vasquez, after an intake visit in about 2 weeks, nothing transferred today. Radiation oncology, Dr Pell, to see him. Next case was the mesothelioma from Dr Ansah's clinic. Coffee ran out by case 6, please could someone tell catering.

Pre-procedure anesthesia, Dr Ellery, port placement 10/9. Kowalczyk S. ASA 3, Mallampati II, dentures upper, NPO since midnight. Apixaban on a planned hold: last dose 10/7 AM, to resume POD1 if the pocket looks dry. Discussed code status in the OR at length with pt and wife Irene. Per policy required reconsideration: his DNR/DNI is suspended for the procedure and the immediate PACU period only, so we may treat reversible anesthesia events, and it goes back into effect automatically on PACU discharge. Pt happy with that and signed the form. Codeine intolerance noted, ondansetron available. Irene asks if they can have the same parking validation as last time, directed to the front desk.

steps.message: Med onc intake, Dr Vasquez. Thanks Dr Sato, I have assumed lead responsibility for Mr Kowalczyk as of this visit, per our call, and she is cc'd. 71M stage IIIA lung adeno. ECOG 1. Retired postal worker, wife Irene (on tamoxifen for her own breast ca, unrelated, she asked me about it). We reviewed plan: carboplatin/pemetrexed with RT, cycle 1 scheduled next week. Folic acid 1 mg daily started today, Rx sent, he had a first dose in clinic, and B12 injection is booked. After a long talk with chaplain Rev. Oyelaran and his daughter he has changed his mind: he wants everything done during treatment. DNR/DNI rescinded, form voided, full code order entered and signed by me 14:20. Atorvastatin continues. Nausea plan reviewed.

Onc pharmacy phone note, D. Whitlock PharmD, re Kowalczyk. 0930: platelets 88 on pre-chemo labs, Dr Vasquez's fellow Dr Amin called asking to swap the apixaban for Lovenox 1 mg/kg q12, I started the order and rang the patient to tell him not to take tonight's dose. 1115: Dr Vasquez reviewed himself, repeat CBC from the same draw re-run at 112, clumped sample. He says leave him on apixaban, no change at all. I cancelled the Lovenox order before it was dispensed, nothing picked up from Walgreens, called the pt back at 1130 and he confirmed understanding: keep taking the same pill morning and evening. Will recheck platelets day 8. Time spent 25 min.

steps.message: Voicemail transcript, auto generated, may have errors. Hi this message is for Dr Feld's nurse, it's Linh, Mrs Pham's daughter, Mai Pham date of birth four twelve fifty one. Mom told me she stopped the sertraline like two weeks ago because it made her tired but I don't know, she might be mixing it up, I found the bottle and it still looks kind of full. Also me and my brother have been talking and we were wondering, should she be a DNR at this point, like is that something we should do, she doesn't really want to talk about it. Please call me back after four. RN comment, T. Hargrove: no contact yet with patient, not verified, will raise at visit next week.

Neurology clinic, Dr Feld. Pham, Mai, 75F, interpreter Mr Dao on the line. Two events since July, both with staring and fumbling, no injuries. Keppra irritability is significant, family describes shouting at grandchildren. We completed the cross taper this week: she took her last Keppra Sunday and is now on Briviact 50 mg BID alone, tolerating it, Rx refilled. If she breaks through I would trial lacosamide, not needed today. Directly confirmed with pt: she stopped sertraline in September on her own, mood fine by PHQ-2 of 0, PCP Dr Bello informed and agrees with leaving it off, taken off the list. Driving: she does not drive. Latex precautions for the upcoming dental work. EEG repeat in spring.

Sunrise Rehab nurse to nurse transfer sheet, RN Coombs. Resident Pham M., room 212A, here 6 days after fall on wet bathroom floor, no fracture, PT 5x/wk going well. MAR header printed from the hospital's August list: levetiracetam 500 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily, but the actual MAR we give from is per the neuro clinic Rx, see binder. Her roommate Mrs Tran in 212B is on warfarin, sulfa allergic, and had a nosebleed last night, no relation, please do not mix up the charts as the first initials confused the night float. Mrs Pham eats well, likes congee from her daughter, wears glasses. Family meeting Thursday 2pm. No new orders from Dr Ostrowski, facility MD.

EMU discharge summary, Dr Feld with fellow Dr Mirza. Mrs Pham admitted 5 days for video EEG, meds weaned during stay. Four typical habitual events captured, including the staring and fumbling her family filmed, with no ictal or postictal EEG change on any. Interictal record normal. Conclusion, reviewed at epilepsy conference by Dr Feld and Dr Nowak: these are functional (psychogenic non-epileptic) seizures, and the previous focal epilepsy diagnosis is withdrawn. Explained in person with Mr Dao interpreting, she took it thoughtfully. Back on Briviact at discharge for now. Intention is to taper it over 4 weeks starting after her next neuro visit, not started. Referral placed to neuropsychiatry, Dr Aguilar, first available in January; Dr Feld remains responsible until seen. Fall precautions.

why: A real HIT allergy and a signed MOLST sit beside a temporary drip, a conditional DNR discussion, a husband's fax and a merely planned warfarin switch.

steps.message: ICU to floor transfer, Dr Benedetti. Lindgren B., 69F, post lap chole complicated by bile leak, ICU 4 days. Got SQ heparin ppx from admission while rivaroxaban was held. Platelets 240 to 71 by day 6, 4T score 7, PF4 positive, SRA strongly positive, so confirmed HIT. Heparin is entered as a severe allergy, all flushes stopped, pharmacy alerted. Ran argatroban gtt 48h as a bridge; it was turned off 0600 today and she is back on her rivaroxaban 20 mg, plt 164 and rising. Adjacent bed 7, Mr Aziz, is the DNR who coded on Tuesday, which family overheard and were upset about, RN Holt spoke with them. Lasix continued. Diet advanced. Dr Reyes updated by phone.

SW note, A. Nakamura LCSW, goals of care conversation with Mrs Lindgren and niece Greta Lindgren, in dayroom. Pt shaken by what she saw in ICU. She said if she ever needed a tube again and was not improving she might not want it, and asked what a DNR would actually mean; Dr Reyes explained. Pt said let's see how the week goes, if she is not better by Friday she would want to look at it again. MOLST form left with her in draft, unsigned, nothing entered in orders. She remains full code today. Greta drives from Duluth, asked about the Medicare days and SNF list. Provided list. Pt asked for a different pillow and her crossword book from home.

Progress note Sat, Dr Reyes. Lindgren. Afebrile, drain out yesterday, walking laps with PT. Euvolemic now, creat up to 1.5, so I stopped furosemide this morning for good, weights daily, no plans to restart unless she becomes overloaded. Niece Greta insists on the phone that Aunt Bea still needs her water pill, explained why not. MOLST: Pt asked to complete it last evening after thinking it over, Friday as she promised herself. Signed by pt and me 18:05: DNR, OK for intubation if reversible. Order entered, copy on chart, she is clear and has capacity. Rivaroxaban continues. PF4 result in allergies confirmed. Home with VNA Monday if PT agrees. Dietary to send soft diet menu.

FAX cover, CareFirst Mail Pharmacy, attn records, 3 pages, pg 2 illegible. RE: LINDGREN. Please update profile and all associated records: rivaroxaban discontinued, warfarin 3 mg daily started, INR clinic Tuesdays, per prescriber. Member name on the claim: Bertil Lindgren, DOB 2/14/1948, spouse on family plan, primary member Beatrice. Clinic RN Sorensen checked: the prescriber on this fax is Dr Haas, Bertil's cardiologist, who has never seen Beatrice, and Mrs Lindgren was reached by phone, she is still on the same blood thinner she came home on, and says Bertil has the pills in a blue box. Fax re-routed to the correct member file, no action on her chart. Dr Reyes informed, pharmacy asked to stop sending to this number.

Pulmonary hypertension clinic, Dr Ruth Abara to Dr Reyes. Thank you for sending Mrs Lindgren, 3 months out from her PE with persistent exertional breathlessness, walks 240 m, no syncope. V/Q shows multiple segmental mismatches unchanged despite adequate anticoagulation; right heart cath 11/2 mPAP 38, PAWR 11, PVR 5 WU. This confirms chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), which now replaces PE as her working principal diagnosis. Going forward many centres favour a VKA, so I plan to discuss changing rivaroxaban to warfarin at her next visit, with the surgical conference first; she remains on rivaroxaban until then and I have written nothing. Referred for PEA assessment at the regional centre. DNR status discussed, she confirms. Aspirin remains listed. Nice to meet her daughter's dog in the photo.

Need to resend the fee schedule, she can't find it. Parking lot gate was broken again.

steps.message: Advisor note, L. Prentiss. Lunch with Geoffrey Thornbury at the club, he had the soup, complained about the new greens fees. Estate attorney Helen Marsh is drafting a revocable trust, expects signing in January, and after that we would need to retitle the brokerage account into it; nothing to do until she sends the executed certification of trust. Reminded him retitling needs medallion or our notary. He muses that one day he might buy a lake house near his brother in Traverse City but nothing concrete and wife not keen. Grandchildren's 529s reviewed, on track. He likes the NVDA run, still aggressive, says no trimming. Send him the article on step up in basis. Follow up after the holidays.

Ops ticket 55120 closed, assigned T. Rowe. Thornbury. Received certification of trust executed 1/15 with notarized signature page, reviewed by legal, OK. Account number retained; registration updated 2/2 from individual to GEOFFREY A THORNBURY REVOCABLE TRUST DTD 1/15, grantor and trustee G. Thornbury, W-9 on file, statement test print fine. Separately, journal request from the same packet: gift of 500 NVDA to son Alistair Thornbury's own account at Schwab, DTC confirm 88410 settled 2/4, remaining NVDA lot here is 1,500 shares. Alistair's account holds his own things and is not ours to record. Paper statement mailing address unchanged. Cost basis carryover form sent. Ticket also had a stray question about e-sign, answered by phone. No other positions touched.

Call log, L. Prentiss, 3/11 09:40. Alistair Thornbury rang the main line, very stressed. Says his father Geoffrey had a stroke on Sunday, is at Munson, cannot speak well, and that he, Alistair, holds power of attorney. Told me to change Dad's risk to conservative straight away and sell everything before the market drops, and to take him off aggressive in your system today, and said he would be very unhappy if anything goes wrong. Asked him to send the POA, which has not arrived; he is unsure which lawyer has it. We cannot act on his instruction, explained that gently. Very sorry to hear this. Called Mrs Thornbury and left a voicemail. Flagged to compliance, officer Dunne. No trading on the account until reviewed.

Compliance memo, P. Dunne, 4/2, re Thornbury trust account. Durable POA dated 2019 and successor trustee acceptance received from attorney Helen Marsh, reviewed by legal; incapacity letter from Dr Sorrell on file. Alistair Thornbury validated as agent. He completed a new suitability questionnaire on behalf of the trust with advisor L. Prentiss. He pushed for conservative, but the 15 year horizon for the grandchildren argues otherwise; supervising principal approved Moderate and that is now the profile. To fund care costs, the entire BRK.B position, 400 shares, was sold 3/30, settled, proceeds in the money market sweep, confirm attached. Added objective on file at his request and with principal approval: funding long-term care for Geoffrey. Education objective stays. KYC on agent complete.

why: A document received is not KYC cleared until a later note, a matured T-bill changes a holding by implication, and a Roth conversion is reversed in the same paragraph.

steps.message: Secure message thread. Keiko Yamamoto: Hi Dana, I emailed my electric bill yesterday for the address thing, so I'm all set now right? Can you mark me as verified, I want to buy something before the fed meeting and my colleague at work said it's instant. Dana Whitfield (service): Hi Ms Yamamoto, got it, thank you, it is in the queue for our CIP review team, which usually takes 3 to 5 business days, and I can't confirm it's accepted until they've looked at it, the bill looks to be older than 90 days so they may ask for another. No trades held for the review besides new purchases. I'll message you as soon as I hear. Keiko Yamamoto: ok thanks, it's the most recent one I have.

Ops daily digest, 10/14, compiled by Dana Whitfield. 1) Yamamura, Kenji: bought 500 TSLA, account ending 2291, not to be confused with the next item as the rep picked the wrong record twice this week. 2) Yamamoto, K., IRA ending 8840: 6 month T-bill CUSIP 912797 matured 10/10, $50,000 redeemed at par and per her standing instruction swept into SWVXX money market, no reinvestment into a new bill. 3) Same client: CIP team accepted the replacement bank statement she sent 10/9 and marked KYC cleared 10/14, reviewer J. Abbott, full trading enabled. 4) Fee schedule reprint on order, expect delay. 5) Reminder: 12/31 RMD report goes out next week, Mr Ito to check the list for clients turning 73.

Advisor note, R. Salazar, call with Ms Yamamoto 11/4. Went through Roth conversion for this year given lower income from her sabbatical. She said yes, let's convert the whole IRA, please start the paperwork, and I drafted the form while we were on the line. She then conferenced in her CPA, Martin Burke, who ran the numbers: bracket jump and no cash outside the IRA to pay the tax. After 20 minutes she said no, forget it, leave it exactly as it is, we can look again next year. Form shredded, nothing submitted to the custodian. Also discussed VYM yield, she's fine. She liked the idea of a moderately aggressive sleeve her friend has but did not want it. Kitchen renovation still underway.

Annual review, R. Salazar. Keiko Yamamoto came in with photos of the condo. She closed on it in August with her savings and a gift from her parents, no IRA money used, and she laughed at our reminder for a home purchase target of 2028, so that objective is finished and comes off. Her new priority, she was clear, is retiring at 60, and she'd like us to plan around that. Our planning software suggested raising equity exposure to reach it; she read the report and declined, she stays conservative, signed the acknowledgment. Monthly contribution stays the max. Beneficiary updated to her sister Hana. VYM still 1,000 shares, money market unchanged. Next review 12 months. She recommended a good dentist on 5th.

Trust and Safety case TS-3320, analyst M. Gallo, 11/20. Papadakis Shipping tenant: our outbound relay was used to send about 80k unsolicited emails on 11/19 from a user seat, in breach of AUP section 4. Under the enforcement policy, and with VP approval from Sarah, the whole account was suspended at 16:40 UTC pending investigation, API and logins disabled. Mr Papadakis notified by phone and email. He says a contractor, Dimitris, had access, and he is furious, threatening to go to his lawyer. Enterprise contract stays in force, plan unaffected. An unrelated customer, Papadopoulos Marine, has a similar ticket which was closed last month. Please route all contact through T&S until the case is resolved. Next review tomorrow 10:00.

Note there's a separate ticket for Papadopoulos Marine, who remain terminated for a different reason, do not confuse them. Mr Papadakis asks for a credit for the day's downtime, routed to AM Ingrid Vos; not agreed so far. CSM to send MFA guidance. Closing T&S case, and normal contact routing resumes.
